sentence: This project designs a way to turn amines into reactive nitrogen forms that directly build bonds between two nitrogen atoms.
This project provides kidney researchers with platforms, approaches and reagents drawn from the physical sciences to find therapeutic targets and treatments for kidney diseases.
This project studies how a mitochondrial protein affects the heart and body weight, using mice that lack the protein in the heart.
This project develops open-source algorithms based on machine learning to model genetic variation and to predict disease risk from genetic and environmental factors.
This project studies how a stress-calming brain circuit that uses somatostatin works in post-traumatic stress and alcohol use disorder.
This project uses planarian stem cells to find out how transposon silencing and chromatin maintenance help them avoid changes with age.
This project studies how food components called glycans can act as prebiotics that help gut microbes grow in undernourished children.
This project develops a fluorescent probe that works with a smartphone to check the quality of zinc supplements at the point of care.
This project builds microscopes and imaging techniques to see how protein diffusion, epigenetic modifications and chromatin work together in the cell nucleus.
This project uses human cells and bioengineering methods to grow human retina tissue for disease modeling, drug screening and transplantation studies.
This project focuses on neuronal degeneration caused by HIV and on ways to understand, treat and prevent it.
This project uses mouse models and somatic genome editing to find lung cancer tumor suppressors and how their function depends on genomic context.
This project builds pangenome graph methods and tools to detect and impute structural variations, and applies them to Alzheimer's disease sequencing data.
This project studies how T cells use force on their surface receptors to detect infected or altered cells and to shape their activation and memory.
This project studies how novel experiences change gene activity in single neurons of the dentate gyrus and how this links to memory function.
This project builds a lipid nanoparticle platform to engineer T cells and tests whether the engineered cells treat tumors in vivo.
This project uses a tonsil organoid model to study how Epstein-Barr virus causes lifelong infection and evades the immune system.
This project supplies tissue, histology and imaging support, including patient imaging, for head and neck cancer research projects.
This project develops a wearable monitor that tracks vital signs to detect blood loss after childbirth early.
This project uses human pluripotent stem cells to recreate intervertebral disc development in the dish and to find how the human disc forms.
